summary: Proceed with no companion. use_atomic_add matters for w13 exactly as much as for w2: in both calls it only changes Marlin's in-GEMM split-K (k-slice) reduction, and that path is active at bs=1 (estimated slice_count >1) but probably degenerate from bs=8 up. The expected bs=1 gain is overstated. The scorer uses a median, so removing a 10/100 slow-mode tail barely moves it, and the fast-mode w13 effect has already measured at about 0. Read the raw bs=1 slow-mode count and p10/p50, not the headline.
justification: WHAT ATOMIC ADD DOES HERE: In Marlin, use_atomic_add only replaces the global reduction of K-slice partials for one (m-block, n-tile) output tile. Without it, partials go through the workspace lock in slice order (barrier_acquire -> fp32 c_tmp read/add/write -> release). With it, slice 0 stores and the other slices atomicAdd bf16x2 into C. It is NOT a reduction over experts or over top_k routes. Both moe_wna16_marlin_gemm calls write one row per (token, route): w13 with top_k=8 rows, w2 with top_k=1 rows. The sum over routes happens later, in _post_norm_combine / fused_post_expert_norm_weighted_sum. So it makes no difference that w13 feeds silu_and_mul rather than a sum: the knob is purely about split-K inside the w13 GEMM (N=2I=8192, K=H=4096). DOES THE PATH EXIST AT THESE SHAPES: At bs=1 under ep8 there is about 1 local route, so 1 m-block (block_size_m 8). That gives 1 x (8192/thread_n = 32-64 n-tiles) x (4096/thread_k = 32-64 k-tiles) spread over a resident grid of 132-528 CTAs (workspace max_blocks_per_sm=4). Each n-tile's K is therefore split across several CTAs, roughly slice_count 4-16. This is an estimate: Marlin's thread_n/thread_k pick and the moe grid size were not read from source, because sglang is not readable on this node. w13 has twice w2's n-tiles, so it slices K about half as deeply as w2 does, and its reduce chain is shorter. At bs=8 (~8 m-blocks x 32-64 n-tiles, about the CTA count), slice_count is about 1-2. At bs=16/32 it is about 1, and Marlin skips the global reduce entirely. So the path exists only at bs=1, plus the bs=4 test, and is marginal at bs=8. EVIDENCE: (1) The old w13-only atomic run (c8ea8e21, 0.987x) was flat at bs=1 (80.23 -> 79.64 us) and its Marlin row was flat. It used the same block_size_m=8, the same workspace and the same w13 call shape at bs=1 as master does now, so its fast-mode reading transfers directly. The w13 reduce chain is worth about 0 us in the fast mode. (2) The landed w2 atomic moved p10 as well as p50 (p10 50.0 -> 46.1, p50 51.4 -> 47.3), so most of its 3.9 us was a fast-mode gain in w2's deeper reduce chain. Only part of it came from the slow mode dropping from 44/100 to 10/100. The hypothesis credits slow-mode removal for w2's gain, which is only partly right. WEAKEST LINK: the expected 44.9 -> 42-43 us at bs=1. A shape's time is the median of paired ratios (TASK.md 'How a run is timed'). A slow mode in 10/100 replays sits entirely above the median, so eliminating it moves the median by only a few tenths of a us. That is below decode_1's ~0.65 us err. The fast-mode component was measured at about 0 in (1). The attribution of the remaining 10/100 to the w13 lock is also unproven. The same +23 us slow mode appeared in the fused bs=1 kernel (41-53/100), which replaced both Marlin calls and had no Marlin lock at all, so at least part of the slow mode is not Marlin's lock chain. Realistic expectation: bs=1 flat to -1 us; bs=8 flat, not 'faster 1-3 us', since w2 atomic moved bs=8 by only -1.6% at z -0.6; bs=16/32 flat (no-op at slice_count 1); bs=128/256 are clean controls. Even a full success at bs=1 is worth well under 1% geomean, inside the headline CI. The hypothesis is still worth one cheap check, because it is the only remaining test of whether the residual bs=1 slow mode lives in w13's lock chain, and the raw replay distribution can answer that.
confounders: w2-marlin-atomic-add-small-m (9080a71): this is the condition being tested, not a confounder to revert. It removed w2's lock chain, so any change in the bs=1 slow-mode count can now be attributed to w13. Reverting it would just repeat the already-measured w13-only run (0.987x, flat). Numerically it stacks: master's w2 atomic path already sits at rel-L2 4.79e-3 vs the non-atomic path, so a self-check gated at 5e-3 against a FULLY non-atomic reference would very likely reject the combination for rounding alone.

sglang-marlin-path-parity: it fixes the workspace (max_blocks_per_sm=4) and with it the resident CTA count, which sets slice_count and the size of any atomic effect. That is unchanged here, so it is a fixed condition and does not confound the run, but the result does not transfer to another workspace setting (cf. marlin-workspace-blocks-per-sm-8, neutral).

triton-map-align-on-block-m-restack / marlin-block-m-two-smaller-on-postnorm: block_size_m at T<=32 (8 at bs<=16, 16 at bs=32) sets the m-block count and therefore the slicing depth. These are unchanged at T<=32, so the comparison is clean. A later small-M block_size_m change (e.g. queued marlin-two-class-block-m-decode32) would change this flag's value at bs=32.

post-expert-norm-triton-small-m: it reads y (cache3, which aliases cache13) at bs<32. A cache13 zero_() before w13 ('atomic_zero') does not reach y, because w2 writes cache3 afterwards, but it does change what w2's no-memset atomic path accumulates onto. If 'atomic_zero' is chosen, w2's self-check premise (C is non-zero when w2 runs) no longer holds, though that only makes w2 safer, not wrong.
interference: No companion. The change is one kwarg on one call at T<=32, plus at most one memset that shows up as its own profile row. The useful readouts are the bs=1 per-shape median, and especially the raw bs=1 timed distribution: slow-mode count out of 100 (master: 10/100), p10 and p50 (master: about 46.1 / 47.3). The prior REWRITE_READ harvest already extracts all of these. The readouts are unambiguous. If the slow-mode count drops to ~0, the w13 lock chain was the residual source, whatever the median says. If it stays ~10/100 and p10 does not move, the w13 knob is retired for good at small M. A median loss of more than 1 us with an unchanged slow-mode count is either the memset ('atomic_zero', visible as a memset row) or slower bf16 atomics; the PATH CHOSEN line says which. ab-revert of w2-marlin-atomic-add-small-m would just reproduce w13-marlin-atomic-add-small-m (already measured, flat). An ab-tune of the workspace would only be informative after a positive result. A control isolating the memset is unnecessary, because the memset has its own row and the w2 run showed the no-memset path passes.
rules_flags: None blocking. The branch is on num_tokens (shape) only; zero_() is a graph-capturable memset; there is no host sync in kernel_fn; the self-check uses synthetic inputs in prepare() and stores only a mode string, never anything derived from data. Weights are untouched.

Precision: two bf16 atomic K-slice accumulations now stack: w13 at slice_count ~4-16 at bs=1, then w2. The judge bound is 1.5% rel-L2 vs FP32 (TASK.md), and master's tests pass at ≤6e-3, so the global margin is fine. The per-row 5x bound on near-zero rows is the one to watch at bs=1/bs=4, where slicing is deepest. Atomics also make outputs nondeterministic in the last bits; that is allowed, but bit-exact cross-run comparisons will not hold.
open_questions: Self-check gate: compare against the CURRENT master path (state['w2_mode'] as chosen, w13 non-atomic), not against a fully non-atomic path, and keep rel-L2 <= 5e-3 for the w13 delta alone. Also log the rel-L2 of the combined path vs a fully non-atomic reference (and, if cheap, an fp32-dequant reference), so a near-threshold rejection is visible. If PATH CHOSEN = master, the run measured nothing and must be harvested as void, not as 'neutral'.

Make the no-memset 'atomic' candidate a real test. cache1 comes from a fresh torch.empty in _forward, which can read as zero in prepare and hide a missing zero. Before the 'atomic' candidate, poison the buffer: e.g. add a self-check-only flag to _forward that fills cache13 with a large finite value or NaN before the w13 call. The w2 run already showed Marlin's moe atomic path needs no pre-zero (C was non-zero and 'atomic' passed), so 'atomic' should win. 'atomic_zero' is a fallback that costs about 1-2 us at bs=1 and would cancel any plausible gain.
Keep use_fp32_reduce=True, as in the spec and as in landed w2. Note the spec wording 'Marlin requires the pair' is not true; it is not required.

Print once from prepare the n-tiles and k-tiles and the resulting slice_count (or at least n_padded/block_size_m and the grid size) for w13 and w2 at T=1 and T=8. If w13 slice_count at bs=1 is <=2, the mechanism cannot work and a flat result is expected, not informative.

Is the residual 10/100 slow mode tied to Marlin at all? The fused bs=1 kernel showed the same +23 us mode with no Marlin lock, so it may be judge-side (clock, cold-L2 flush interaction). If this run leaves it at ~10/100, stop attributing it to lock chains.

Correct the expected rows before harvest: bs=8 should be 'flat', not 'faster', and the kill criterion should read the raw slow-mode count and p10, not only the median, because a median metric cannot see a 10% tail.
